one_line: Access-lineage infrastructure for investigating and containing compromised SaaS sessions without destroying trusted access.
what_it_does: Records credential ancestry, lets a human and agent investigate incident branches, simulate containment, and execute an explicitly approved revocation plan.
leverage_rationale: Structured, incident-scoped lineage and containment operations materially change the security workflow; a general UI-driving agent would struggle to reliably discover descendants, preserve trusted branches, and produce an exact approved execution plan.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes tracing sessions to API keys, application grants, child tokens, and secondary sessions.
Agent uses authenticated incident-scoped tools with no secrets returned.
Human approval gates execution and the agent verifies every targeted credential afterward.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually coherent end-to-end evidence from credential creation through failed session-only revocation, investigation, simulation, approval, execution, and verification.
execution_evidence: Transcript explicitly walks through a live deployment scenario and a fresh isolated account.
Permanent receipt and post-execution checks are described.
Screenshots visibly show sessions, API keys, account protection, and an unrecognized-login incident.
impact_rationale: Account takeover recovery is a concrete high-stakes problem, and preserving legitimate access while containing descendants is a credible security benefit for SaaS operators and users.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies independent persistence paths created by compromised sessions.
Workflow addresses both containment and operational lockout impact.
creativity_rationale: The Git-like access-lineage mental model and human-governed branch containment are a memorable, ambitious application of WebMCP to security infrastructure.
creativity_evidence: Persistent directed credential graph is central to the concept.
Containment strategies are simulated before a one-time execution capability is issued.
usability_note: Strongly guided incident workflow with explicit human approval; security complexity is appropriate to the problem.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and unusually complete evidence for a consequential workflow.

one_line: A shared evidence room where agents investigate claims and people decide what becomes a source-bound receipt.
what_it_does: Exposes narrow tools for claim/source inspection, comparison, and pressure testing, then stages a visible packet for human adoption, challenge, or discard.
leverage_rationale: Structured claim IDs, source mappings, uncertainty, and pressure tests create shared state that is substantially more reliable than UI scraping, while authority remains with the person.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies five page-scoped investigation tools and a staging tool.
Agent and person share exact identifiers and uncertainty classifications.
Tool surface cannot choose or confirm the receipt.
execution_rationale: The design is coherent and carefully scoped, but the demo link is dead and there is no transcript; evidence supports a strong claimed prototype rather than a fully demonstrated workflow.
execution_evidence: Description covers investigation, staging, human decision, and browser-local SHA-256 receipt.
Packet states the registered tool path ends at staging.
impact_rationale: Evidence quality and authority boundaries are valuable for research, fact-checking, and consequential knowledge work; the unit-distance example makes the need concrete.
impact_evidence: Specific distinction between an internal model counterexample and independently verified mathematics.
Receipt records integrity without overstating truth or certification.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-room metaphor, staged packet, and explicit human authority boundary are a fresh synthesis for agent-assisted research.
creativity_evidence: Source-bound receipt and pre-registered pressure test.
Visible separation of uncertainty, missing proof, and authority.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow, though the dead demo limits confidence in actual interaction quality.
red_flags: No transcript and no gallery images
standouts: Human confirmation is not simulated as agent authority
advance_reason: Strong concept and leverage; advance despite limited runtime evidence.

one_line: Turns large public-comment corpora into briefs with excerpts traceable to source records.
what_it_does: Lets agents search Regulations.gov and pin exact excerpts to a shared evidence board while an analyst verifies or removes them before cited export.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured search, pinning, and shared review state, but a capable general agent could achieve much of the workflow with browser/API interaction at meaningful friction.

Agent reads analyst decisions before preparing the brief.

execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive.
About text describes search, pin, verification/removal, and cited brief stages.
impact_rationale: Policy analysts and researchers have a real need to synthesize thousands of comments while preserving traceability; the workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific Regulations.gov research use case.

creativity_evidence: Agent and analyst jointly curate source excerpts before export.
usability_note: Verification gate and shared board should reduce citation mistakes; actual polish is not evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video frames or transcript
standouts: Source traceability is part of the export workflow

one_line: Maps benefits cliffs for a household and lets users probe which rules cause them and how changes heal them.
what_it_does: Computes income/benefit maps, traces cliffs to eligibility rules, overlays life changes, and exposes shared human-agent probes over the chart.
leverage_rationale: A person cannot practically operate the large rules engine directly, while structured probes let an agent perform precise causal and counterfactual analysis beside the shared chart and log.
leverage_evidence: Description says the person cannot drive a 600MB rules engine.
Tools knock programs out, trace eligibility flips, search safe regions, and find smallest rule changes.
Human and agent actions land in a shared log.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a deep, coherent analysis workflow and includes three frame sheets, though no transcript and no live observation limit certainty.
execution_evidence: About text covers household input, map, causal probes, counterfactual overlays, and healed cliffs.
Gallery/frame evidence was submitted.
impact_rationale: Benefits cliffs are a real, high-stakes problem for families and policymakers; explaining causes and testing legal changes could provide substantial practical and policy value.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies families losing thousands from small income changes.
Product maps what a Colorado family keeps and identifies responsible programs/rules.
creativity_rationale: Applying mechanistic-interpretability-style probes to the benefits system is an original and ambitious interaction model with meaningful depth.
creativity_evidence: Knockout, tracing, and minimal-intervention probes are first-class user operations.
On-screen cliff healing makes policy counterfactuals tangible.
usability_note: Stepwise probes and visual shared log are well matched to a complex domain.
advance_reason: Top-tier impact and transformative agent leverage.

one_line: A Chrome extension that exposes legacy SaaS APIs as WebMCP tools while retaining page context.

leverage_rationale: The extension can make otherwise unsupported legacy SaaS accessible through structured tools, though it is primarily an adapter/convenience layer and depends on existing APIs.
leverage_evidence: Description exposes vendor API operations as agent tools.

Architecture targets SaaS that cannot add native WebMCP.
execution_rationale: The concept and claimed framework are coherent, but no video frames/transcript and little concrete end-to-end evidence limit execution credit.
execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive.
Showcase extension was presented to a future user, according to the packet.
impact_rationale: There is a concrete audience of merchants using unsupported legacy B2B SaaS, and an extension could extend useful software without vendor redevelopment.
impact_evidence: Packet cites hundreds of thousands of daily merchants for the target legacy system.
Vendor need not modify the SaaS.
creativity_rationale: A browser-level WebMCP uplift for legacy SaaS is a useful and ambitious infrastructure direction, though adapter patterns are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Converts an existing MCP server into an extension and proposes a reusable extension framework.
usability_note: Potentially powerful, but BYOK/security/sandbox complexity and absent visual evidence leave usability unclear.

advance_reason: Promising infrastructure idea, but claimed execution is too thin relative to stronger entries.

leverage_rationale: Semantic tools over a shared scene document make precise spatial edits and inspection practical; pixel-based UI driving is substantially less reliable for geometry and dimensions.

Live demo reported alive.
impact_rationale: Apartment renters, buyers, and designers have a real need to test whether furniture fits and circulation remains livable before committing.
impact_evidence: Pitch names bed fit, dining circulation, and livability as concrete planning problems.

creativity_evidence: Agent and person collaborate on the same editable scene document.
Illustrative sunlight and camera controls extend beyond a basic floor-plan editor.
usability_note: Visual editing plus semantic actions is a strong fit for iterative planning.
